title: Deployment Orchestra — Setlist & Hourglass Log (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This working doc frames a lightweight, repeatable deployment "orchestra" for small-to-medium feature releases. The aim is pragmatic: a human-readable setlist (roles + timed cues), an hourglass timeline for preflight/launch/postflight activities, and a compact post-release scribe template so we capture decisions and fallout quickly.

Scope:
- Target releases: API surface changes, configuration rollouts, model routing updates that require gradual traffic shifts.
- Not for critical infra migrations or schema-only DB migrations (separate blast-wave runbooks).

Hourglass timeline (compact):
- T minus 72h: Draft release notes + risk statement. Notify stakeholders.
- T minus 48h: Smoke test matrix published. Load test smoke run (if applicable).
- T minus 24h: Code freeze for the release train; feature flags confirmed.
- T minus 4h: Preflight sync (30m) — owners, telemetry, rollback thresholds.
- T minus 1h: Readiness checklist run by steward and SRE.
- T plus 0—+30m: Canary window: route 1% -> 5% traffic ramp, automated health gates at 1,5,15 minutes.
- T plus 30—+180m: Ramp to target (50%/80%/100%) depending on signal.
- T plus 3—+24h: Postflight sampling, quality evals, cost signal sanity check.

Roles & Setlist (short):
- Conductor (release owner): coordinates setlist, owns go/no-go.
- Watcher (observability): watches dashboards, surface regression signals, initiates rollback triggers.
- Steward (team lead): runs preflight checklist, triages immediate errors.
- Traffic Maestro (routing/infra owner): performs traffic shifts and monitors capacity.
- Scribe: captures timeline, links to issues, and records actions taken.
- On-call Engs (as needed): prepared to patch or revert.

Preflight checklist (to run T minus 4h -> T minus 1h):
- [ ] Release notes published and distributed (owner + product).
- [ ] Rollback plan verified with measurable trigger points.
- [ ] Canaries built & smoke tests passing against canary track.
- [ ] Feature flags verified and toggle playbook ready.
- [ ] Capacity headroom checked for peak TTL/latency percentiles.
- [ ] Alert burn-in list created (which alerts are expected and which indicate real regressions).
- [ ] K/V cache warming notes done (if applicable).
- [ ] DB migrations (if any) are backward-compatible and staged.

Launch choreography (minute-by-minute condensed example):
- 00:00 Conductor announces start, Scribe starts timestamped log.
- 00:01 Traffic Maestro moves 1% to new variant. Watcher starts 0-1m micro-checks.
- 05:00 If no critical errors, ramp to 5%. Scribe notes any anomalies.
- 15:00 Gate check: error rate, p99 latency, business signal. If green, ramp to 20%.
- 45:00 Ramp to 50% unless cost or stability signals require pause.
- 90:00 Ramp to 100% and begin postflight sampling.
- If any gate fails, follow rollback matrix immediately (see Rollback Triggers below).

Rollback triggers (examples — must be numeric where possible):
- Error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points over baseline sustained for 5 minutes.
- p99 latency increase > 2x baseline sustained for 10 minutes.
- Business signal degradation (key metric drop > 4% within 30m).

Variant stitching & fallback:
- Prefer model-compat variants (quantized vs full) over rolling back the entire feature when output quality tolerates it.
- If fallback variant is used, flag user requests for downstream QA sampling.

Observability & dashboards to watch (minimum):
- Service-level error rate (5m / 1h), p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU util per pool.
- Cost delta per token / per request (sampled hourly).
- Model-quality quick-check: a small set of golden prompts and automated scoring.
- User-facing error surface (synthetic transactions).

Post-release scribe template (fill quickly within first 2 hours):
- Release ID / Tag:
- Owner / Conductor:
- Time window (start / end):
- Canaries: start %, ramp steps, final %.
- Signals observed (good/bad): short bullet list.
- Actions taken (pause/ramp/rollback/patch): timestamped.
- Residual tasks & follow-ups (who + due date).
- Link to incidents / PRs / telemetry charts.

Observer diary (example entries):
- 2025-03-18 10:01 — Canary 1%: no errors, p99 +5% (within tolerance).
- 2025-03-18 10:07 — Ramp 5%: spike in gRPC errors +0.8pp; investigation shows transient serialization timeout on vGPU node pool; throttled back to 2% and notified infra.
- 2025-03-18 10:22 — Mitigation: added extra retry backoff; error rate returned to baseline after 4m; resumed ramp.

Open questions / decisions to make before next run: (owner initials)
- Do we treat model-version bumps under this rhythm or require a cold-roll runbook? (M.C.)
- Validate whether cost delta alerts should be automated (suggest threshold: 20% hour-over-hour). (D.A.)
- Should the Traffic Maestro have delegated authority to exceed 50% in low-risk windows? (P.K.)

Quick checklist for release notes (one-paragraph starter + bullets):
- Short summary of change (one line).
- Why: business rationale & risk summary.
- What to watch: enumerated metrics/alerts.
- Rollback plan & contact list.
- Known limitations and mitigations.

Appendix: small utilities and links
- Canary smoke script: github.com/redwood/release-scripts/tree/main/smoke-checks
- Golden prompt set: confluence link above.
- Rollback snippet examples (kubectl / traffic API commands) — see linked PR.

Notes: this doc is intentionally compact for quick consumption during launches. It should evolve to include one-click checklist links from the Console once the Runbook UI is available. For now, please use this as the canonical short-form setlist and scribe template for mid-sized rolls.

Action items (short):
- D.A. to prototype cost-delta alert thresholds against last 3 months of traffic by 2025-03-25.
- P.K. to confirm delegated ramp authority and document in team charters by 2025-03-28.
- L.O. to extract rollback commands into a single-run script and link in this doc (due 2025-04-01).

End of draft.
